title: CCPA / CPRA California consumer privacy rights
why: California's CCPA and CPRA require notice at collection, verifiable consumer access and deletion within statutory deadlines, opt-out of sale or cross-context behavioural sharing (including Global Privacy Control signals), and non-discrimination when rights are exercised.

addRequirements.title: Notice at collection lists every category and retention period
addRequirements.statement: When personal information is collected from a consumer, the application shall disclose the categories collected, the business purpose, whether each category is sold or shared, and its retention period.
addRequirements.definition: Every personal field gathered from a {secondary} maps to a disclosed CCPA category and retention policy before ingestion.
addRequirements.failurePath: If an undisclosed category is submitted for collection, the application rejects ingestion with a typed policy error rather than storing undisclosed data.
acceptance: Given a collection payload with an undisclosed personal category, when ingestion is attempted, then the application rejects it with a stable code.
Given the collection register, when exported, then each category names purpose, sale-or-share status and retention duration.

addRequirements.title: Do-Not-Sell-or-Share and Global Privacy Control stop downstream sharing
addRequirements.statement: When a consumer opts out of sale or sharing or sends a Sec-GPC signal, the application shall persist the opt-out immediately and suppress all third-party advertising or cross-context data sharing.
addRequirements.definition: A browser signal (`Sec-GPC: 1`) or one-step opt-out choice binds without forcing account creation and overrides marketing dispatch.
addRequirements.failurePath: If a downstream sharing sink is invoked for an opted-out consumer, the call is blocked and recorded in the privacy audit trail.
acceptance: Given a request carrying `Sec-GPC: 1`, when processed, then sale-and-sharing is disabled without requiring sign-in.
Given an opted-out consumer, when an analytics or ad-sharing export runs, then their record is excluded and the suppression is logged.

addRequirements.title: Verifiable consumer access and deletion cover stores and service providers
addRequirements.statement: When a verified consumer submits a right-to-know or right-to-delete request and no statutory exemption applies, the application shall export or delete their personal information and propagate deletion to registered service providers.
addRequirements.definition: Requests carry an auditable verification record, 45-day deadline clock and downstream propagation receipt.
addRequirements.failurePath: If a statutory exemption or legal hold blocks deletion, the application refuses deletion for the exempt scope only and returns the named exemption.
acceptance: Given a verified right-to-delete request with no hold, when executed, then primary records are deleted and provider deletion tasks are enqueued.
Given a record under a statutory exemption, when deletion is requested, then the exempt reason is returned and non-exempt data is still deleted.

addGates.statement: Consumer right-to-know, right-to-delete and Sec-GPC opt-out are exercised by automated tests against owned stores.
